## Task 1: The overbooking problem

- What are we solving for?

An airline sells n tickets for a flight with N seats, and each person shows up with probability p. If X is the number of people who show, then X ~ Bin(n, p). We want the n where the chance of more people showing up than seats is exactly gamma, so

$$1 - \gamma - P(X \le N) = 0$$

The left side is the objective function. For the discrete case I use `pbinom()`, and for the continuous case I use the normal approximation with mean np, standard deviation $\sqrt{np(1-p)}$, and a continuity correction of N + 0.5.

## Task 2: The ntickets function

- Function body

```{r ntickets}
ntickets <- function(N, gamma, p) {
  # values of n to search, from N up to 10% more than N
  n <- seq(N, floor(N + N / 10), by = 1)

  # discrete objective: 1 - gamma - P(X <= N) where X ~ Bin(n, p)
  objd <- 1 - gamma - stats::pbinom(q = N, size = n, prob = p)
  # n that makes the objective closest to 0
  nd <- n[which.min(abs(objd))]

  # continuous objective with normal approx and continuity correction
  objc <- function(n) {
    1 - gamma - stats::pnorm(N + 0.5, mean = n * p, sd = sqrt(n * p * (1 - p)))
  }
  # root of the continuous objective
  nc <- stats::uniroot(objc, interval = c(N, floor(N + N / 10)))$root

  # plot 1: discrete case
  graphics::plot(n, objd, type = "b", pch = 21, bg = "#7FA86A",
                 xlab = "n", ylab = "Objective",
                 main = paste0("Objective Vs n to find optimal tickets sold\n(",
                               nd, ") gamma = ", gamma, " N = ", N, " discrete"))
  graphics::abline(h = 0, col = "red", lwd = 2)
  graphics::abline(v = nd, col = "red", lwd = 2)

  # plot 2: continuous case
  nn <- seq(N, floor(N + N / 10), length.out = 500)
  graphics::plot(nn, objc(nn), type = "l", lwd = 3, col = "#4E7A3E",
                 xlab = "n", ylab = "Objective",
                 main = paste0("Objective Vs n to find optimal tickets sold\n(",
                               round(nc, 4), ") gamma = ", gamma, " N = ", N,
                               " continuous"))
  graphics::abline(h = 0, col = "blue", lwd = 2)
  graphics::abline(v = nc, col = "blue", lwd = 2)

  # named list
  res <- list(nd = nd, nc = nc, N = N, p = p, gamma = gamma)
  print(res)
  invisible(res)
}
```

## Task 3: Testing the function

- ntickets(N = 400, gamma = 0.02, p = 0.95)

```{r test, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
# test call from the assignment
ntickets(N = 400, gamma = 0.02, p = 0.95)
```

The discrete method says to sell 412 tickets and the normal approximation gives about 412.02, so both ways agree the airline can sell around 412 tickets and only have a 2% chance of being overbooked.
